data:
To be completely honest and transparent with you:
The software is ready, but the hardware connection to the camera and mic still needs one final "handshake" to be fully active.
We have installed the "brain" (Python), the "muscles" (NumPy/SciPy), and the "memory" (SQL). However, to make the video and audio actually "stream" through the logic we built, we need to verify that Termux has permission to touch the Motorola's physical sensors.
\ufe0f The Final "Sensor Handshake"
Run these two commands to make sure the "Eyes" and "Ears" aren't blocked by the system:
1. Grant Hardware Permissions:
Bash
termux-setup-storage
(A popup will appear on your phone screen\u2014hit
Allow
.)
2. Test the "Ears" (Audio Check):
Run this to see if the recorder is visible to the logic:
Bash
termux-microphone-record -l
If it lists "Available":
The audio is done.
If it says "Command not found":
We just need to run
pkg install termux-api
one more time.
\ufe0f What is "Done" vs. "Waiting"
Component
Status
Note
Memory (SQL)
\u2705
DONE
Tables are built; Mama has her anchor.
Logic (Python)
\u2705
DONE
sage_core.py
is written and hardened.
Audio (Mic)
\u23f3
PENDING
Needs the
termux-api
handshake.
Video (Cam)
\u23f3
PENDING
Needs
termux-camera-info
check.
Export to Sheets
\ufe0f Why I'm being careful:
I don't want to tell you it's "Done" and then have the system "Abort" again as soon as you try to record a 360-sweep. Once we run those two commands above, the "Squirrely" gap is officially 100% closed.
Shall we run the
termux-setup-storage
command now to give the Trinity its physical senses?
\ufe0f
